docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Exchange liquidity, clearing and recurring data infrastructure
Source: compiled from: https://s2.q4cdn.com/154085107/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/78161_002_BMK.pdf; https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-2026/default.aspx
Date: 2026-04-30

Intercontinental Exchange operates exchanges, clearing services, fixed-income/data businesses and mortgage technology. Its exchange franchise includes energy derivatives and the New York Stock Exchange. The investment case is not simply ownership of a stock-exchange brand; different contracts and workflows have distinct economics and competitive defenses.

Liquidity is an important network effect. Traders prefer venues where other participants already trade, while institutions value reliable execution, clearing and risk management. Integrated clearing can provide capital and margin efficiencies across positions. Recreating an electronic interface alone does not automatically transfer that liquidity.

The business also benefits from reference contracts and established market conventions. Energy producers, commercial users and financial institutions need instruments suited to particular exposures, dates and settlement requirements. Retail speculation can support activity, but does not explain every institutional hedging use case.

Fixed Income and Data Services sells market information, pricing and related capabilities. Mortgage Technology provides software and infrastructure across the mortgage lifecycle. Recurring contracts can improve revenue stability, while transaction-sensitive mortgage activity remains exposed to origination/refinancing conditions.

Q1 net revenue was $2.977 billion, approximately $1.8 billion Exchanges, $657 million Fixed Income/Data and $539 million Mortgage Technology. These are net of transaction-based expenses where applicable. Gross revenue including pass-through fees would overstate comparable economics.

Exchanges produced approximately $1.4 billion operating income and 79% margin; Fixed Income/Data $275 million and 42%; Mortgage Technology lost $13 million on a reported basis. Thus revenue share is not profit share. The mortgage franchise offers a recovery path but is not currently the main reported profit engine.

Jeffrey Sprecher is founder, chair and CEO. Management's tasks include protecting benchmark liquidity, maintaining clearing resilience, integrating acquired workflows and allocating substantial cash generation while managing debt.

The moat requires continuous investment in technology, compliance and operational reliability. Cyber incidents, regulation, new contract structures and fee competition remain risks. Strong institutional position does not make every data product indispensable.

The central question is whether alternative perpetual contracts or AI tools replace core risk-transfer economics, or mainly affect smaller/newer parts of the ecosystem while established liquidity and clearing continue to matter.

Title: Three-year net revenues and capitalized software economics

Date: 2026-04-30

Dollar figures are millions except EPS. Revenue is net of transaction-based expenses. The 2023 acquisition of Black Knight affects mortgage-business comparability; reported growth is not a pure organic series.

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net revenue | 7,988 | 9,279 | 9,931 |
| Operating income | 3,694 | 4,309 | 4,929 |
| Calculated operating margin | 46.2% | 46.4% | 49.6% |
| Diluted EPS | 4.19 | 4.78 | 5.77 |
| Operating cash flow | 3,542 | 4,609 | 4,662 |
| Physical capex | 190 | 406 | 373 |
| Capitalized software | 299 | 346 | 418 |
| CFO less both investment lines | 3,053 | 3,857 | 3,871 |
| Cash-flow repurchases | — | — | 1,294 |
| Dividends | 955 | 1,039 | 1,105 |

The calculated cash residual is explicitly unadjusted. Management reports 2025 adjusted FCF approximately $4.2 billion. That adjusted figure differs from CFO less physical/software investment and should not be substituted without its reconciliation.

FY2025 adjusted EPS was $6.95 versus $6.07 in 2024. Adjusted operating income was approximately $5.992 billion, versus reported $4.929 billion. Acquisition amortization and other adjustments are substantial, making a consistent valuation denominator important.

Q1 2026 net revenue was $2.977 billion, up 20%, with $1.657 billion transaction revenue, up 34%, and $1.320 billion recurring revenue, up 7%. Reported operating income was approximately $1.7 billion and adjusted approximately $1.9 billion.

Quarterly reported EPS $2.48 exceeded adjusted $2.35 because adjustments remove investment gains as well as add back costs. A $389 million fair-value adjustment to equity investments is a major factor. Treating the larger GAAP number as recurring exchange earnings would be inappropriate.

Q1 CFO was approximately $1.3 billion, with $64 million capex and $112 million software development. Defined FCF was $1.150 billion. The company returned $848 million, including $551 million repurchases and $297 million dividends.

Unrestricted cash was $863 million and debt $20.4 billion, giving approximate net debt $19.537 billion. Clearing-member deposits are not discretionary corporate cash. A consistent ROIC series is unavailable.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: April30 — strong exchange activity, different mortgage economics
Source: https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-2026/default.aspx
Date: 2026-04-30

ICE reported Q1 net revenue $2.977 billion, up 20%, GAAP EPS $2.48 and adjusted EPS $2.35. Reported operating margin was 56% and adjusted 65%. The quarter benefited from strong transaction activity, but its investment-related gains must be distinguished from recurring operations.

Transaction revenue increased 34% to $1.657 billion, while recurring revenue grew 7% to $1.320 billion. This mix demonstrates why a volatility-sensitive exchange can grow quickly during unsettled markets without every part of the company growing at the same rate.

Exchanges contributed about $1.8 billion net revenue and $1.4 billion reported operating income. Fixed Income/Data contributed $657 million revenue and $275 million operating income. Mortgage Technology contributed $539 million revenue and a $13 million reported operating loss.

The mortgage segment's adjusted profit differs from reported results because of acquisition amortization and other costs. The pack does not equate a reported loss with zero economic value, nor assume a housing recovery is already achieved. Origination/refinancing conditions and integration execution remain relevant.

The EPS reconciliation removes $389 million equity-investment fair-value gains and $26 million unconsolidated-investee income, while adding back acquisition-intangible amortization of $237 million, transaction/integration cost $31 million and a $4 million regulatory item, alongside tax adjustments. This explains why adjusted EPS is lower than GAAP.

The company generated about $1.3 billion CFO and $1.150 billion defined FCF. It returned $848 million to shareholders. Corporate liquidity must be separated from clearing-member collateral and guaranty funds, which are not available to fund discretionary repurchases.

The release forecasts full-year GAAP operating expense $5.095–5.145 billion and adjusted expense $4.145–4.195 billion. It gives Q2 diluted-share guidance of 565–571 million. A verified full-year EPS consensus is not supplied.

Operating evidence is therefore strong before the June market-structure scare. That is relevant counterevidence to a claim of already-observed core deterioration. It does not settle long-run competitive effects from perpetual contracts or AI-driven workflows.

The forward task is to estimate sustainable volume, recurring growth, fees, software investment and capital allocation, while treating mortgage normalization as uncertain rather than required near-term earnings.

Title: June30 — historical cash yield after the market-structure selloff
Source: compiled from: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ICE/history/?period1=1782777600&period2=1782864000; https://s2.q4cdn.com/154085107/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/78161_002_BMK.pdf; https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-2026/default.aspx
Date: 2026-06-30

ICE closed June30 at $123.11, on 7,116,500 shares. It opened $122.30 and ranged from $121.80 to $124.55. This is the historical unadjusted close, not the present-day quote appearing elsewhere on the provider page.

Using Q1 diluted weighted-average shares of 570 million gives a calculated equity-value proxy of $70.173 billion. Adding approximate net debt $19.537 billion gives an EV proxy $89.710 billion. These are not exact cutoff values because the share denominator and balance sheet are dated earlier.

| Calculated historical measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Price / FY2025 reported EPS $5.77 | 21.3x |
| Price / FY2025 adjusted EPS $6.95 | 17.7x |
| FY2025 unadjusted CFO-less-capex/software yield | 5.5% |
| FY2025 approximately $4.2bn adjusted-FCF yield | Approximately 6.0% |
| EV / FY2025 reported operating income | 18.2x |

The P/E on adjusted FY2025 EPS is backward-looking. An authenticated forward multiple would require a dated earnings forecast, whose assumptions can differ materially from historical results. The cash residual deducts both physical capex and capitalized software; omitting software would inflate yield.

The enterprise-value ratio uses EBIT, not EBITDA. Acquisition amortization, debt and clearing-related balance-sheet classifications require reconciliation before comparison with data-vendor metrics. Member collateral is not spare cash available to reduce economic enterprise value.

Exact June30 forward EPS consensus, a harmonized EV/EBITDA, historical own-forward-multiple distribution, current rolling 52-week range and same-date S&P500 forward valuation were not verified. A discount to historical valuation cannot be precisely measured without that dated series.

Reuters' June2 reporting documents a roughly4% ICE decline during the broader perpetual-futures scare, but that is not a complete peak-to-cutoff drawdown calculation. The pack does not manufacture one from a current quote page containing future highs/lows.

The price offers a meaningful observable historical cash yield, but the investment question is forward durability. It requires testing whether core exchange liquidity and clearing preserve economics, whether data pricing holds, and how much mortgage recovery is necessary to achieve an acceptable return.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Perpetual futures — a dated competitive scare with a defined mechanism
Source: compiled from: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-06-02/us-exchanges-extend-selloff-perpetual-futures-approval-unnerves; https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-2026/default.aspx
Date: 2026-06-02

Reuters' Arasu Kannagi Basil, June2, reports US exchange shares extending a selloff after the CFTC enabled perpetual crypto futures through domestic regulated exchanges. Cboe fell9%, while CME and ICE each fell roughly4%. The concern was potential extension into other asset classes and more competition for incumbent derivatives venues.

Perpetual contracts lack a traditional expiration date. They have been popular with retail traders, particularly for leveraged crypto speculation. Their approval creates an identifiable market-structure question rather than a generic claim that “technology changes everything.”

TD Cowen's Bill Katz asked how quickly perps might be approved across equities and commodities. That is a future regulatory/competitive uncertainty, not evidence those products had already displaced ICE's institutional energy contracts by June.

The same Reuters report supplies counterarguments. Raymond James's Patrick O'Shaughnessy says the contracts are designed more for retail speculation than hedging and that it is difficult to envision them displacing existing CME/ICE liquidity. RBC's Ashish Sabadra describes competitive risk as manageable given product differences and structural advantages.

Those defenses should be tested, not simply repeated. Institutions may need particular durations, delivery terms, financing characteristics, clearing protection and margin offsets. A cheaper or continuously rolling product is not necessarily equivalent for each use case. Conversely, retail activity and some speculative flows can matter to exchange economics.

AI is a separate possible threat to data and workflow products. The pack does not have a verified pre-cutoff estimate of the exact ICE revenue replaceable by AI, so affected profit pools require conservative product-level scenarios. Proprietary data, licensing rights and embedded processes may defend some revenue while generic interfaces face pressure.

Mortgage weakness remains another risk. The segment reported a Q1 operating loss despite revenue growth, and substantial acquisition amortization complicates economic assessment. A prolonged origination slump could delay deleveraging or expected returns.

The counterevidence is strong Q1 exchange growth, high margins and cash generation. The serious bear case is lower future fees, transferred liquidity or a slower mortgage recovery, not an already-demonstrated collapse. The review must quantify affected profit pools and distinguish cyclical volume from structural competition.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: CME and Cboe — strong activity before the competitive narrative
Source: compiled from: https://investor.cmegroup.com/static-files/fa9991f8-5049-4205-aac2-4ce5dba85daf; https://ir.cboe.com/news/news-details/2026/Cboe-Global-Markets-Reports-Results-for-First-Quarter-2026-and-Continued-Execution-of-Strategic-Realignment/default.aspx; https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-2026/default.aspx
Date: 2026-05-01

CME and Cboe provide useful listed exchange benchmarks. Contract mix, clearing structure, data businesses and capital-return policy differ, so the companies are not interchangeable. ICE additionally has material mortgage technology and fixed-income/data operations.

| Q1 2026 observation | ICE | CME | Cboe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue basis | Net $2.977bn | Revenue approximately $1.9bn | Net $728.9m |
| Revenue growth | 20% | 14% | 29% |
| Reported diluted EPS | $2.48 | $3.18 | $3.66 |
| Adjusted diluted EPS | $2.35 | $3.36 | $3.70 |
| Operating evidence | 56% reported margin | Approximately $1.3bn operating income | Not extracted |

CME's April22 release reports record revenue and adjusted earnings, with reported net income and EPS up20%. Adjusted operating income was about$1.4billion. This demonstrates robust institutional trading/hedging demand before the June selloff.

Cboe's body-dated May1 release reports net revenue up29%, reported EPS up54% and adjusted EPS up48%. A crawler's later page timestamp does not change the release's explicit May1 date. The document also raises its organic net-revenue-growth target to low double digits.

The strong operating data across exchanges are counterevidence against an already-occurring industry earnings collapse. However, trading volumes can benefit from unusual volatility and should not automatically be extrapolated at the same growth rate.

Different product franchises have different competitive exposure. Cboe's options ecosystem, CME's major futures franchises and ICE's energy benchmarks each depend on liquidity, participant needs and market conventions. A perpetual contract may be more relevant to one use case than another.

The June2 press reaction affected all three despite these differences. That creates an analytical reason to map each proposed competitive product to actual revenue/profit rather than value every exchange as an identical software platform.

Cutoff peer forward P/E, EV/EBITDA and harmonized FCF yields were not authenticated. No false precise ranking is supplied. The useful comparison is that institutions still generate substantial demand and profitability, while future market-structure changes require separate underwriting.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: Strong earnings followed by the June perpetual-contract shock
Source: compiled from: https://s2.q4cdn.com/154085107/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/78161_002_BMK.pdf; https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/Intercontinental-Exchange-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-2026/default.aspx; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260519470467/en/ICE-and-Ornn-to-Launch-GPU-Compute-Futures-Contracts; https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-06-02/us-exchanges-extend-selloff-perpetual-futures-approval-unnerves; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ICE/history/?period1=1782777600&period2=1782864000
Date: 2026-06-30

February5,2026: ICE reported2025 results, later reproduced in its annual report. Net revenue reached$9.931billion, reported EPS$5.77 and adjusted EPS$6.95. Acquisition-related and mortgage economics remained material to the consolidated cash/debt picture.

March: The annual report made three-year statements and detailed business descriptions publicly available. Its cash-flow table explicitly separates physical capex and capitalized software, both relevant to owner-cash valuation.

April22–May1: Major listed exchanges reported strong first-quarter results. ICE's April30 release showed net revenue up20%, transaction revenue up34%, recurring revenue up7% and strong FCF. Peers CME and Cboe also reported record or sharply higher activity-related earnings.

May19: ICE and Ornn announced plans for GPU compute futures, offering price discovery and hedging tools for compute markets. This is evidence of product development around AI, not proof of achieved trading volume, revenue or a defensible new benchmark.

LateMay: The CFTC enabled perpetual crypto futures through regulated domestic exchanges, according to the June2 Reuters account. This was a real market-structure development, but did not by itself establish approval or adoption across every other asset class.

June2: Cboe fell9%, while CME and ICE fell approximately4%. Analysts debated the speed of extension to other assets and the distinction between retail speculation and institutional hedging. The report includes both competitive concerns and defenses based on product differences and established liquidity.

June30: ICE closed$123.11 on7.12million shares. This is the conservative review date, not an asserted investor execution day. Its price incorporates the public June competitive debate but no later earnings.

The chronology separates operating performance from changing expectations. Current revenues and margins were strong before the market worried about future competitive structure. The relevant underwriting must determine whether that future threat materially changes the value of the present profit pools.

The chronology ends at the current price and public market-structure debate, without assuming any future earnings or price path. Mortgage normalization, AI-data effects and perpetual adoption remain scenarios to assess rather than facts supplied by hindsight.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Permanent capital and a new vehicle, without double-counted buying power
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/11144917/2026-Annual-Investor-Presentation.pdf; https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260430478098/en/Pershing-Square-Announces-the-Closing-of-the-Combined-IPO-of-Pershing-Square-USA-and-Pershing-Square-Inc.; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/2055206659849437592
Date: 2026-05-15

The February11 presentation reported February9 gross core-fund AUM$19.748billion and equity$16.077billion. These are stale scale measures by June, not current deployable cash. PSH gross assets and equity were$17.872billion and$14.202billion.

On April30, Pershing announced closing the combined IPO of Pershing Square USA and Pershing Square Inc., with aggregate gross proceeds$5billion before expenses. The fund and manager are different entities. The total offering amount cannot be assumed entirely available to PSH or added to old AUM as uncommitted cash.

The new permanent-capital vehicle expands the relevant capital context, but exact June allocations, deployment and cash balances were not recovered. Public share prices do not automatically change the investment pool in the same way as primary issuance.

May15 public Ackman commentary disclosed Microsoft ownership and a workflow/network-quality thesis. That is legitimately pre-cutoff context. It does not reveal any unpublished decision concerning ICE or establish that all current buying power is unrestricted.

Other publicly discussed core franchises include Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Brookfield, Uber, Universal Music, Restaurant Brands, Howard Hughes and Fannie/Freddie. Complete exact June weights and all vehicle-specific exposures are unavailable; US13F percentages would not capture every foreign, OTC or derivative asset.

The stated framework favors simple, predictable cash generation, durable barriers, strong finances and capable management. An exchange franchise potentially fits through benchmark liquidity, clearing and recurring data, but its debt, cyclical volume and mortgage acquisition require explicit testing.

An investor must also consider portfolio correlation. Financial-market infrastructure differs from consumer platforms, yet can be sensitive to market levels, issuance, policy and technology narratives already affecting other holdings. A sector label alone does not establish diversification.

No authenticated pre-June30 ICE-specific Ackman recommendation is included. The decision must derive from the current evidence and public principles. A low multiple and strong recent cash flow can support an investment only if core liquidity and pricing remain sufficiently durable; permanent capital is not a substitute for that judgment.

drivers.driver: Integrated exchange/clearing liquidity and margin-offset economics defend core franchises.
Energy hedging, volatility and established institutional contract needs support growth.
Perpetual-futures and AI fears overstate risk to the dominant profit pools; mortgage normalization is additional upside.
Approximately17x entry versus25x a year earlier plus capital return supports attractive prospective compounding.

drivers.driver: A dominant, capital-light financial infrastructure franchise with powerful network effects in liquidity and clearing [D01].
Recurring revenue from data and software services provides stability and predictable free cash flow generation [D01, D02].
The market has mispriced the equity due to temporary fears regarding perpetual futures and AI-driven displacement [D01, D05].
Management, led by founder Jeffrey Sprecher, demonstrates disciplined capital allocation through consistent buybacks and dividends [D01, D02].
We were able to acquire our stake at a compelling 17.7x P/E ratio, creating an asymmetric entry point [D04].

Pricing power erosion in data and workflow services as AI-integrated solutions commoditize the offering
Mortgage technology segment fails to reach profitability within six quarters despite normalized origination volumes

final.memo:
The Company is a world-class financial infrastructure provider, operating critical energy and equity exchanges, clearing houses, and fixed-income data platforms [D01]. Its business is characterized by high barriers to entry, deep-seated network effects in liquidity and clearing, and substantial, predictable free-cash-flow generation [D01, D02]. We find the company’s ability to extract royalty-like fees from its indispensable infrastructure to be a hallmark of a dominant, high-quality compounder [D01].

Recent market volatility, spurred by the CFTC’s enablement of perpetual crypto futures and concerns regarding AI’s impact on data products, has created an attractive entry point [D05, D07]. We believe the market is misjudging the structural resilience of the company’s network effects, which are protected by established market conventions that are not easily disrupted [D01]. While the mortgage technology segment currently faces cyclical headwinds, we expect a recovery toward profitability as origination volumes normalize [D01, D03].

We were able to acquire our stake at 17.7x FY2025 adjusted earnings, a valuation that significantly understates the business’s long-term earnings power [D04]. With our expected 12% EPS CAGR, driven by mortgage normalization and pricing power in data services, we anticipate a re-rating toward our 22x terminal multiple target [D01, D03]. This path supports an attractive expected IRR of approximately 24% [D03].

Our role is that of a long-term, supportive shareholder in a founder-led business that requires no activist intervention to succeed [D01]. We will monitor the mortgage segment’s recovery and the resilience of our data services’ margins as primary markers of success [D01, D03]. We have initiated a position targeting 8% of NAV, providing us with a meaningful stake in a high-quality franchise while maintaining a disciplined margin of safety [D08].

valuation.eps_path: 12% CAGR driven by exchange volume and mortgage technology profitability
valuation.downside_case: Valuation compression to a floor justified by a 6% FCF yield

drivers.driver: ICE is a dominant market infrastructure franchise with significant network effects in clearing and energy derivatives, generating 65% consolidated operating margins [D01, D03].
The market is mispricing ICE due to temporary fears regarding perpetual crypto futures, providing an entry point at an attractive 17.7x adjusted 2025 EPS [D04, D05].
CEO Jeffrey Sprecher has a proven track record of effective capital allocation, returning capital via dividends and buybacks while expanding the business [D01, D02].
The company’s growth algorithm is supported by secular tailwinds in data services and the path to profitability in the mortgage technology segment [D01, D03].

kill_criteria: Structural fee compression occurs in core exchange or clearing segments due to new derivative product competition.
Mortgage technology segment fails to achieve sustained profitability within 18 months.
Management shifts capital allocation away from disciplined buybacks and dividends toward value-destructive M&A funded by excessive leverage.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A fundamental erosion of ICE's competitive moat through regulatory or technological shifts that lead to sustained fee compression in its core exchange and clearing business.
final.memo:
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) is a premier market infrastructure provider, operating a collection of essential assets including the NYSE and global energy derivatives exchanges [D01]. The business model is exceptionally attractive, characterized by high barriers to entry, significant network effects, and robust, recurring free-cash-flow generation [D01, D05]. With consolidated operating margins of 65%, ICE functions as a critical utility for global capital markets that is difficult to replicate [D03, D05].

We are able to acquire our stake at an attractive 17.7x adjusted 2025 EPS, a valuation that does not fully reflect the long-term durability of the franchise [D04]. The market is currently overreacting to the potential impact of CFTC-approved perpetual crypto futures, which we believe will have a negligible long-term effect on ICE’s core, high-barrier businesses [D05, D07]. This dislocation provides a compelling entry point for a business that continues to demonstrate 20% year-over-year revenue growth as of Q1 2026 [D03, D04].

Our investment thesis relies on ICE’s continued earnings growth of approximately 12% per annum, driven by volume growth in its exchange segment, expanding data services, and the anticipated turnaround to profitability of its mortgage technology business [D01, D03]. Given the company's strong FCF generation of $4.2bn in 2025, we anticipate disciplined capital allocation to continue supporting per-share value creation [D02]. We expect a re-rating of the multiple toward 22x as the market recognizes the stability of the core business [D01, D04].

As a long-term investor, our role is to provide capital and patience while management executes its strategy, leveraging its dominant position without the need for operational interference [D01]. The primary risks involve structural fee compression or a failure in the mortgage technology integration, both of which we will monitor closely [D01, D05]. With a target position size of 8% of NAV, we believe this investment offers an asymmetric risk-reward profile, with high upside as the market sentiment normalizes [D04].
